- Several deadlines missed without clear mitigation updates to the stakeholders.

What I’m asking for (high level):
1) Clear 30/60/90 milestones with measurable outcomes (see template).
2) Twice-weekly 30-min syncs with me to review blockers and progress (calendar invite to follow).
3) Weekly status notes in the shared doc (link below) summarizing actions taken and outcomes.

Please prepare the 30/60/90 draft using the template and share by EOD Monday (2026-11-16). I want us to be explicit about success criteria so we can decide if additional support or role adjustments are necessary.

I recognize you’ve had a heavy load — this is intended to be supportive and time-boxed. If you feel any of the milestones are unrealistic, flag them in your draft with alternatives.

Thanks,

Alex — good questions. Answers inline below and I’m attaching a filled example to illustrate specificity I’m asking for.

1) Feature flag rollout: Demonstrating a reliable mitigation plan plus a committed, realistic timeline is acceptable. The key success criteria are: (a) test coverage for the rollback path, (b) stakeholder sign-off on revised timeline, (c) no regression incidents in staging for two full sprints.

2) Sync cadence: Twice-weekly 30-mins is preferred for the first 30 days to build momentum. If you show consistent progress after 30 days we can reduce frequency to once weekly.

Expectations for the 30/60/90 draft (use the template):
- 30d: unblockers removed, clear plan for outstanding tasks, one stakeholder sign-off delivered.
- 60d: majority of outstanding work delivered; measurable improvement in delivery predictability (e.g., on-time completion rate > 80%).
- 90d: sustain improvements for two consecutive months; hand-off plan for any outstanding items.

Next steps:
- Please upload your draft to the shared doc by EOD today (2026-11-16).
- I’ll book the standing 30-min syncs on Tuesdays/Thursdays 10:00–10:30 PT starting 2026-11-17.
- Monica will support documentation and will join the weekly readouts as needed.

I’m copying Monica to ensure we have the plan captured in People Ops notes.

Best,
Rachel
